what_it_drives: OpenMM molecular dynamics simulations with GROMACS pdb2gmx topology preparation under a Charmm36m force field, dispatched through Parsl to local V100 GPUs and to Polaris/ALCF A100 nodes via the PBS queue
failure_handling: not stated for the driven code - no recovery mechanism is described for a failed or non-convergent simulation. The version of record does report three agent-level failures it does not handle. Hallucination: with only five search results returned, "it fetched PDB IDs of 148L, 1B7E, 1LYZ, 2LYZ, 3WEL, 5R2Z, 7BVM, and 7F26 ... These PDB IDs were hallucinated by the LLM agent, as only 5 search results were generated from the researcher", and "Based only on the model context, it failed to provide correct information for the following simulation runs." A scaling limit: "the number of tool calls that LLM agent made were capped around 24, with 100 simulations specified in the input prompt during the experiment", worked around by moving parallelism inside a single ensemble tool rather than by recovery. And scheduler behaviour: "The tasks waited in the queue for ~265 minutes, until 25 nodes were available", with "~177 seconds difference in execution time" of load imbalance between workers

what_it_drives: OpenFOAM-v2406 case directories - solver dictionaries and control files generated, the solver executed, and post-processing utilities run
failure_handling: the corrector agent analyses error logs and iteratively prompts for adjustments until successful completion; the authors report the average number of correction iterations increases as flow complexity rises, and unrecovered cases count against the success rate

what_it_drives: DOLFINx 0.10.0 finite-element solves with Gmsh mesh generation and PETSc linear algebra, driven through a HeatConfig JSON configuration posted to a FastAPI endpoint
failure_handling: the residual 2.2% of runs fail on invalid boundary condition combinations, mesh resolution requests exceeding GPU memory, and numerical divergence on stiff transients; a debug_simulation tool and a 25-step ReAct budget bound the retry loop

what_it_drives: VASP 6.6 and Quantum ESPRESSO pw.x DFT calculations and HydraGNN, UMA, MACE and NequIP interatomic potentials driven through ASE relaxations, with jobs submitted via SLURM on Frontier and Perlmutter and PBS on Aurora
failure_handling: not stated

what_it_drives: AVEVA Process Simulation 2025 flowsheets through a Python MCP server - the C1 Water Methanol Separation distillation model in case studies 1 and 2, and an ammonia synthesis flowsheet with branched topology and a recycle loop in the stability case study
failure_handling: the convergence-sensitive step is deliberately withheld from the agent: "At this stage, a critical manual intervention is required because the user must shift the distillation column setup from 'Configure' mode to 'Solve' mode to obtain rigorous simulation results. This step is intentionally delegated to the human user rather than the LLM agent because it frequently triggers convergence issues that experienced process engineers can quickly diagnose and resolve." The authors add that "both inexperienced users and LLM agents often struggle to obtain a converged simulation flowsheet when switching on rigorous simulations in the distillation column model", and that the design "avoids forcing the agent to handle challenges that may exceed its current capabilities". Advanced convergence troubleshooting is named as future functionality, not present

what_it_drives: an ASE Langevin-thermostat NVT molecular dynamics run using the MACE-POLAR-1-M interatomic potential, preceded by RDKit SMILES-to-XYZ conversion and a Packmol periodic box build
failure_handling: the authors describe only agent-level failure, not driven-code failure: the common failure mode in which a specialist transfers control back to the supervisor without performing any work, mitigated by a fixed execution rule and a recursion limit of 25 hops. What happens when the molecular dynamics run itself fails is not stated

what_it_drives: KBase applications executed as jobs in the KBase Narrative platform - FastQC read QC, SPAdes assembly, Prokka and RAST annotation and GTDB-Tk taxonomic classification
failure_handling: a self-correction loop in which the Validation and Handle Error nodes iteratively refine parameters to resolve runtime failures without human intervention; if human-in-the-loop approval is enabled the agent pauses and waits for confirmation or revision

what_it_drives: legacy FEniCS finite element Python scripts, generated and then executed by the Executor agent
failure_handling: the Executor returns run-time output and errors to the Coder agent; the loop continues until the code executes without errors or the LLM reaches its token limit, so it is bounded by the token budget rather than by a convergence check

what_it_drives: Python/CVXPY convex-optimisation programs solved by a designated convex or conic solver, executed inside a fixed validation harness
failure_handling: on validation failure the code, execution logs, validation report and frozen contracts are returned to the experiment agent for bounded repair, with the budget explicitly capped at two contract-repair rounds, three experiment-code repair rounds and three final review-repair rounds; solver non-convergence specifically is not addressed

what_it_drives: OpenFOAM case directories (0/, constant/, system/ dictionaries and Allrun scripts), Gmsh mesh generation scripts, ParaView/PyVista scripts and Slurm submission scripts on Perlmutter
failure_handling: the Reviewer Agent performs error contextualisation, reviews the trajectory of previous attempts and generates structured modifications to the problematic files, repeated until the errors are resolved or a user-specified maximum number of attempts is reached

what_it_drives: OpenFOAM case dictionaries (0/, constant/, system/fvSchemes, system/fvSolution) for simpleFoam, rhoCentralFoam and sonicFoam runs on NACA 0012 airfoil and de Laval nozzle grids
failure_handling: on failure the agent triggers an autonomous error-reflection loop iterating up to 30 times, parsing the execution log and configuration files to pinpoint the error location and root cause; 7% of cases were terminated after failing to resolve errors within the 30-round limit and a further 32% halted on divergence or unphysical results

what_it_drives: an OpenEvolve evolutionary program-search loop over a reduced-order fracture-network forward model, and ObsPy-based seismic subroutines - STA/LTA and an ML phase picker, the Geiger location method, Richter magnitude and an ETAS forecasting model

what_it_drives: SIESTA 5.4.2 input files - mesh cutoff, basis size, k-grid, force and energy thresholds, vacuum spacing - and variable-cell relaxation runs for pentagonal 2D monolayers
failure_handling: non-converged calculations trigger an automated Diagnostician agent that parses error logs and extracts supporting failure lines; the relaxation loop is capped at six iterations and a four-hour wall-clock budget per target, and malformed agent proposals are programmatically overridden with physically consistent fallback parameters and logged

what_it_drives: OpenFOAM 10 case input files (0/, constant/, system/ dictionaries) and the Allrun execution script for eight tutorial-derived cases
failure_handling: on error the Runner passes the failing command and error context to the Reviewer, which examines the file architecture and returns revised instructions to the InputWriter; the loop repeats until no errors occur or a user-defined maximum iteration or token budget is reached. Non-convergence is scored rather than repaired - executability 2 means the case is runnable but does not converge

what_it_drives: a CityLearn V2 building-control environment coupled step by step to Pandapower and OpenDSS power-flow models of low-voltage feeder networks, with EnergyPlus invoked for custom building datasets and Stable-Baselines3 controllers trained inside the loop
failure_handling: detected violations or failures are converted into structured feedback that triggers targeted code updates, additional retrieval and regeneration in an iterative loop until a stable executable simulator is obtained; separately, grid contingencies that result in divergence or violation of network limits are classified as unsafe and counted

what_it_drives: OpenFOAM cases driven through Foam-Agent, including modification and wmake compilation of case-local C++ turbulence-model source - a runtime correction to the Spalart-Allmaras model
failure_handling: when a verification gate rejects a run the rerun controller revises the requirement, and may reuse nearby successful cases such as relaxation factors or schemes

failure_handling: the Reviewer node runs three sequential LLM calls - an analysis call producing a diagnosis from the extracted error set, a plan call turning it into a minimal rewrite plan, and a rewrite call realising the edit - with the explicit gap that errors bypassing the FatalErrorIn macros fall outside the extractor

what_it_drives: not stated - the authors drive nothing themselves; the paper names software that agents could drive and reports that the cited RECOIL prototype drives freight simulations and the Gurobi solver

what_it_drives: Quantum ESPRESSO input decks, LAMMPS molecular dynamics scripts, RASPA3 Monte Carlo simulations and MACE machine-learned potentials, with ASE and pymatgen for structure handling
failure_handling: if clear issues are detected, such as a lack of DFT convergence, the Operator terminates the run and attempts to reconstruct or optimise the input parameters; a separate Evaluator gates task completion and discards failed attempts from context

what_it_drives: Quantum ESPRESSO input files submitted through SLURM, plus Phonopy phonon calculations, UMA and MACE pre-relaxations and PORMAKE framework construction, on named materials including Si, MgO, Cu, Pt, CsPbI3 and LiFePO4
failure_handling: if any calculation fails, the DFT subagent troubleshoots the issue by modifying the input files and passing the revised files to the running subagent for resubmission

what_it_drives: MOOSE multiphysics input decks and the MOOSE executable that runs them
failure_handling: the agent re-reads the MOOSE error output and rewrites the input in an execute-analyze-correct loop capped at three rounds; the authors report the dominant failure mode is that all unsuccessful attempts were caught in an infinite loop, the agent repeatedly trying to fix an error by calling a particular function

what_it_drives: LAMMPS input and simulation scripts - 127 simulation and 40 modelling scripts in the training corpus - executed inside a Docker container
failure_handling: escalation to the human rather than automated recovery - when the agent is unable to complete a task independently it can pause the current process and request clarification or assistance from the user

what_it_drives: COMSOL Multiphysics models built by emitting Java API calls for geometry, materials, physics interfaces, mesh, study and export, executed from Python via JPype and MPh
failure_handling: the agent receives execution feedback and a fitness score and proposes a corrected solution; the authors note the dominant failure is silent, where the partially constructed model exports nothing or an incorrect value

what_it_drives: Quantum ESPRESSO v7.4 input decks and executable chains from pw.x through ph.x, q2r.x and matdyn.x, launched with MPI/OpenMP on local servers or Slurm-managed clusters
failure_handling: configurations that fail to achieve convergence are treated as invalid points in the accuracy-cost space and excluded from Pareto consideration - non-convergence is scored as an invalid point rather than repaired

what_it_drives: ASE and CHGNet structure relaxations over candidate CIF files, plus pymatgen space-group and structure-matching analysis, invoked from LLM-synthesised Python; VASP DFT is used for evaluation rather than driven by the agent
failure_handling: runtime errors produce a diagnostic error signal that triggers the Tool Code Generator to revise and regenerate the code; the generated relaxation code itself wraps each structure in try/except

what_it_drives: PyQUDA measurement scripts and SLURM job-submission scripts run against the CLQCD C24P29 gauge ensemble, including gauge loading, multi-grid solver setup, sequential-source propagators and MPI data layout
failure_handling: routine errors such as einsum index mismatches, gauge-context lifetime errors and array-shape problems are detected by static analysis or test execution and corrected automatically; residual errors surface only at the numerical-comparison stage, which the authors name as the primary failure mode the critique-rewrite pipeline did not fully catch

what_it_drives: an orb-v3 machine-learned-potential formation-energy oracle with relaxation, the Chemeleon crystal structure generator and a MACE ranking surrogate, inside the MADE environment, with pymatgen convex hulls defining the reward
failure_handling: not stated

what_it_drives: scikit-learn workflow functions invoked as schema-validated actions through an adapter layer; no domain simulator or solver is driven
failure_handling: when an action fails the execution engine records the failure type, error context and partial outputs in the trace and enters a failure-aware control loop rather than terminating unconditionally; each recovery attempt is logged as a new action node and a maximum of 10 steps is enforced

what_it_drives: an Aspen Plus flowsheet - a shortcut column then a rigorous RadFrac column with sensitivity analyses and design specifications, then a heat-pump-assisted flowsheet with compressor, heat exchangers and splitter - written as generated input files and run through Aspen Plus API commands
failure_handling: not stated

what_it_drives: an established commercial process simulator, unnamed - digitised flowsheet graphs are systematically translated into its simulations and then parameter-fitted unit by unit
failure_handling: convergence failures are resolved by simplifying the flowsheet, and the simplification is logged rather than hidden

what_it_drives: Python numerical libraries called from generated, executed programs - SciPy solve_ivp for ODE and DAE integration, NumPy and Matplotlib - plus the Wolfram Alpha and Stack Overflow APIs; no process simulator or flowsheet is driven
failure_handling: if code generation raises an error the result includes the error message, the faulty code snippet and the error trace identifying the specific tool causing the error; the framework localises the offending call, regenerates the program using that tool documentation and prior history, and repeats until the program executes successfully or reaches a maximum number of iterations

what_it_drives: OpenFOAM v2406 case files inside a Docker container - blockMesh and snappyHexMesh meshing, boundary-condition and scheme dictionaries, the icoFoam and multiphase solvers and the generated Allrun script - plus ParaView output and generated Python plotting scripts
failure_handling: the module captures detailed error logs and contextual information about the failure and structures this feedback for the LLM, which is fed back along with the original case prompt and system constraints, creating a closed-loop process that iteratively improves configurations until successful simulation

what_it_drives: a MACE-LAMMPS coupled build on Frontier using the ACEsuit LAMMPS fork with the ML-MACE package, Kokkos and HIP gfx90a targeting; a 20,000-step ASE MACE molecular-dynamics trajectory; OpenMM AMOEBA NPT simulations at 1 fs timestep and 1 ns per replica launched eight replicas to a single srun; a Spack environment building CP2K with GPU support; and distributed MACE training across two to eight GCDs
failure_handling: the agent recorded missing batch-environment commands, compile-mode incompatibilities and ASE HIP out-of-memory behaviour; the authors note a Spack and cray-mpich linkage failure detectable "only after extensive debugging" and argue that future tools should treat negative evidence as a first-class object

what_it_drives: OpenFOAM-v2406 case directories - system/controlDict, fvSchemes and fvSolution, the 0/U initial fields, boundary conditions and an execution script - for the icoFoam, simpleFoam, pisoFoam and pimpleFoam solvers
failure_handling: the runner monitors real-time logs and on error the corrector analyses and resolves the issue, resubmitting the corrected files in a cycle until the simulation completes; a run counts as failed if it does not reach a convergent solution within 72 hours or 10 correction attempts

what_it_drives: OpenFOAM 10 cases run through MetaOpenFOAM 2.0 - the PitzDaily RANS case, CounterFlowFlame2D, BuoyantCavity, homogeneous isotropic turbulence and a two-dimensional hydrogen combustion chamber on a 50x50x1 grid run with reactingFoam - plus scipy.optimize L-BFGS-B and an active-subspace sensitivity and response-surface library
failure_handling: not stated

what_it_drives: FEniCSx, NGSolve, scikit-fem and DUNE-fem through Python, deal.II through C++, 4C Multiphysics through YAML input decks, Kratos Multiphysics through JSON and FEBio through XML, plus Gmsh for mesh generation and preCICE for coupling
failure_handling: the documentation instructs the agent to consider an alternative solver if the simulation fails after multiple attempts, the knowledge base covers nonlinear convergence criteria and failure-signal paths explicitly, and a results critic must use the validation action to check for NaN, constant fields and suspiciously large values

what_it_drives: designed to drive pycalphad multicomponent equilibrium calculations, ESPEI Bayesian MCMC database assessment and the kawin precipitation-kinetics module over MCP tool contracts, but in the reported work these were run by the authors own scripts rather than by an agent
failure_handling: not stated

what_it_drives: OpenFOAM v10 cases - 110 basic cases derived from 11 reference OpenFOAM cases with ten parameter variations each, plus 16 advanced cases including a two-obstacle case - and standalone Python PDE solvers for the coding benchmark
failure_handling: the reviewer agent supports a trial-and-error loop mimicking human troubleshooting; the authors analyse the failure taxonomy explicitly, finding that retrieval mitigates configuration errors such as missing physical properties or undefined keywords while the reviewer reduces reasoning and consistency errors such as mismatched boundary conditions

what_it_drives: OpenFOAM case directories and binaries - solver selection across compressible and incompressible, steady and transient regimes including simpleFoam, rhoCentralFoam and pisoFoam, turbulence-model and thermophysical files, and fluentMeshToFoam mesh conversion - with literature reproductions of a NACA0012 airfoil and a supersonic nozzle
failure_handling: errors are typed and routed: general errors, over 70% of runtime errors, go through suspicious-file detection, error confirmation, retrieval of related tutorial files and file modification; persistent errors trigger a reflection module that writes structured insights into long-term memory, and correction is capped by a maximum reflection-iteration limit

what_it_drives: LAMMPS input decks executed via MPI or Kokkos on GPU resources, using embedded-atom-method interatomic potentials enumerated with atomman and downloaded from the NIST interatomic potentials repository, plus Python post-processing code written by the URSA execution agent
failure_handling: on error the agent invokes a second language model with the full history of previously generated LAMMPS scripts and their errors, iterating until the simulation succeeds or a user-specified iteration limit is reached, with the terminal output showing the initial script and each subsequent edit

what_it_drives: FSL, FreeSurfer, fMRIPrep, QSIPrep and ANTs neuroimaging pipelines over BIDS-organised ADNI, HCP Young Adult and UK Biobank data, inside pinned Python environments and Docker containers
failure_handling: post-execution verification uses expected-artifact checks, missing-file detection, NaN and Inf screening and quality-control validation, with session-level checkpointing and resumability; nothing is stated about what happens when a driven tool errors or a pipeline diverges

what_it_drives: SurFF facet ranking, VSSR-MC surface-reconstruction Monte Carlo, AdsorbDiff placement, two-phase climbing-image nudged elastic band on the UMA universal machine-learned potential, slow-growth molecular dynamics, and the CatMAP microkinetic solver and electrochemical kinetic Monte Carlo, on Ni(111), Cu(211), Ni5Ga3, hcp-PdMo, MoS2, Mo2C and Ni on titanium-oxide slabs built from bulk crystal input
failure_handling: when a nudged-elastic-band run fails to converge or an endpoint is rejected by the deterministic gate, the validation auditor diagnoses overlap, element-count or path-collision causes and proposes targeted geometric corrections feeding the next iteration, looping up to ten times; barriers outside a physically plausible window return to redesign, and non-convergent or non-physical paths are retried through an adaptive ladder and screened by a post-run validator

what_it_drives: OpenFOAM v10 case directories - the constant, system and initial-field dictionaries such as thermophysicalProperties and blockMeshDict - and the OpenFOAM meshing and solver utilities blockMesh, snappyHexMesh, rhoCentralFoam and pimpleFoam, plus Gmsh through its Python API
failure_handling: the agent is directed to use OpenFOAM error logs to identify the first failure and apply corrective actions, illustrated by switching an unsupported mixture type after the log reported an unknown mixture; but on high-speed combustion setups the agent "often triggered solver crashes or divergence and did not consistently converge to a stable configuration through log-driven edits alone"

what_it_drives: LS-DYNA-format keyword decks run through the OpenRadioss solver - three cervical spine segments from the VIVA+ model, a head-neck complex from Stemper et al. 2004, and a Taylor bar impact deck
failure_handling: the solver energy-balance and mass-error diagnostics are parsed and gate scoring, so a model that terminates but violates energy conservation is not scored as trustworthy; repairs are confirmed by a disposable scratch-probe re-run before being proposed; unknown error codes fall back to conservative human escalation; and in the sweep agent each point has an independent pass or fail path

what_it_drives: the TamGen structure-conditioned molecular generator, Uni-Dock and AutoDock-Vina-family docking, ADMET-AI property prediction, Fpocket binding-site detection, BioPython receptor preparation and RDKit and pandas post-processing, on CrossDocked2020 protein-ligand complexes
failure_handling: if the final candidate count falls below the requested number the controller expands the generation budget on a predefined recovery schedule and repeats processing, evaluation, selection and validation; generated wrappers get at most two refinement attempts after evaluator feedback; and once the retry budget is exhausted the workflow returns an explicit partial-delivery status

what_it_drives: Ansys HFSS three-dimensional full-wave models of quad-flat-no-lead packages - geometry, materials, lumped terminal ports, a solution setup at 1 gigahertz with a convergence tolerance of 0.001 and an interpolating sweep from 1 megahertz to 8 gigahertz - driven through the PyAEDT Python API, with scikit-rf and a SPICE netlist writer downstream
failure_handling: not stated - the only related text is that PyAEDT is used to launch a simulation and monitor convergence status; nothing is said about the response to a failed or non-converged solve

what_it_drives: PandaPower AC power flow, optimal power flow and N-1 contingency screening on the IEEE 118-bus and smaller test cases, ANDES time-domain transient stability runs with a three-phase fault at the point of interconnection, and ParaEMT short-circuit-ratio screening, with PSS/E supported through the same solver-agnostic base class
failure_handling: the intended fail-safe default is abstain-and-escalate: on solver non-convergence, missing inputs or ungroundable numerics the agent routes to human review rather than issuing an approval recommendation; the contingency tool runs a baseline power flow first and raises an explicit error on non-convergence; and the capacity search reverts to a coarse range scan when a monotonicity contradiction is detected

what_it_drives: Aspen Plus V14 backup flowsheets through the COM API - reading and writing stream and block data, building blank flowsheets into simulatable ones from a declarative spec, running them to convergence and running techno-economic analysis; an equation-oriented optimisation package and an external costing framework are orchestrated but not bundled
failure_handling: an automatic taxonomy classifies each attempt as success, syntax, hallucinated path, wrong type, non-convergence, silent wrong or timeout; harness-level COM crashes are mitigated by retrying once on a fresh sandbox subprocess; a restart tool kills and reopens a wedged session; hung generated scripts are force-terminated after a timeout; and tool errors naming the available fields are described as diagnostic and acted on

what_it_drives: real constraint-solver libraries invoked from an agent-written Python program in a persistent kernel - python-sat for SAT, python-sat RC2 for MaxSAT, z3-solver for SMT, cpmpy for constraint programming, clingo for answer-set programming and didppy for domain-independent dynamic programming
failure_handling: not stated beyond a default thirty-step cap before stopping and the logging of execution failures in an optional per-episode statistics file; submissions are syntax-checked server-side before being stored

what_it_drives: OPM Flow simulation decks - keyword editing, deck setup and run launching - plus in-house Python optimisation code running genetic-algorithm and particle-swarm well-placement searches on the Brugge benchmark model
failure_handling: self-healing logic proactively fixes convergence issues and input errors with an optional human in the loop, and a job manager monitors health to eliminate dead time from unexpected failures

what_it_drives: EnergyPlus 22.2.0 input files for the NREL iUnit modular building - the agents write individual input objects, run the simulation and read the resulting error file to repair severe and fatal errors
failure_handling: when an error is detected the debugging agent analyses the simulation error file to identify the problematic class and object, and the loop runs until no errors remain, with the agent recalling previous error messages to inform each subsequent iteration

what_it_drives: GEOS XML input decks - schema-valid files of several hundred lines covering solvers, constitutive models, meshes, geometry, boundary conditions, events and outputs - for a carbon-dioxide sequestration benchmark, plus the GEOS runs themselves and their output fields
failure_handling: the simulator rejected the first input deck twice, and both diagnoses - a geometric conflict and an interface subtlety - were applied and persisted to a runtime-error knowledge base so later decks benefit; a bounded review loop re-invokes the producing agent with corrective feedback up to three times

what_it_drives: EnergyPlus input files and simulation runs - specifically the five-zone air-cooled example file, edited for lighting power and envelope solar gains and re-simulated for a baseline-versus-retrofit comparison, with weather files and output variables managed through the server
failure_handling: not stated

what_it_drives: EnergyPlus 25-1-0 input files for the NREL iUnit - named objects and fields including material thickness, building orientation, glazing and insulation parameters, edited through a Python input-file library - with the baseline and nine modified runs launched against a fixed weather file
failure_handling: all simulations completed except one intentionally invalid glazing configuration, which the authors present as fault-tolerant behaviour; prevention is the stated mechanism, with the rule-based agent enforcing object-field consistency and preventing ill-formed edits that commonly cause simulation failure in manual workflows

what_it_drives: EnergyPlus input files of the NREL iUnit - envelope and infiltration objects edited into three retrofit alternatives and nine single-parameter variants covering orientation, window area, roof insulation thickness and material properties - each simulated against a Golden, Colorado weather file
failure_handling: not stated - each run produces error logs and the discussion notes that agentic workflows "require well-specified objectives and robust error handling", but the paper never states what the system does when a simulation fails

what_it_drives: OpenSeesPy finite-element models of three-dimensional frame structures, built from a language-model-generated JSON schema of geometry, materials and design actions
failure_handling: on a runtime error such as a stiffness-matrix singularity or non-convergence the server identifies the failure stage - input validation, execution or numerical solution - and delivers both a machine-readable report and a human-readable explanation

what_it_drives: topology-optimisation problems from an engineering benchmark suite - a two-dimensional beam problem and a two-dimensional photonics problem - plus conditional generative and diffusion model training jobs submitted to a Slurm cluster over SSH, and a Prusa 3D printer
failure_handling: not stated; the only failure observation is behavioural degradation on long workflows, where the agent ceases to issue further calls

what_it_drives: ECLIPSE-format reservoir input decks executed by the OPM Flow simulator - the SPE1, SPE9 and Norne models - inside an optimiser loop with a weighted normalised root-mean-square-error objective
failure_handling: the parameterising agent validates the input deck by dry runs at the minimum and maximum substituted values, and any error such as a non-monotonic relative permeability curve or an unsupported arithmetic expression is relayed back before the optimisation starts

what_it_drives: a 30-query black-box optimisation loop over three objectives - the Rosenbrock analytical function, a machine-learning hyperparameter-tuning objective and a robot-pushing control simulator - with the agents replacing the acquisition function rather than the surrogate
failure_handling: not stated

what_it_drives: pyGIMLi, SimPEG, ResIPy and PyHydroGeophysX electrical-resistivity-tomography forward modelling and inversion runs - standard, time-lapse difference and structure-constrained inversions - on field ERT and seismic refraction data from three named sites, plus PyDaymet climate retrieval and a Monte Carlo petrophysical conversion
failure_handling: a regular-expression fallback parser extracts key fields when the model returns ill-structured responses, preventing run-stopping failures, and file parser exceptions handle misidentified data formats; the author names invalid JSON configurations and misidentified formats as the typical failure cases encountered during development

what_it_drives: Aspen Plus steady-state flowsheets through the COM API - blocks and streams created and connected, feed and block specifications set, the sequential-modular solver run to convergence, and stream tables, capital and operating costs and an optimised operating point extracted
failure_handling: failures are made recoverable in-loop by design: "an invalid connection request returns the valid ports for the target block; an unrecognized input tag returns the block's valid fields; a feed-specification call reports which component flows were applied and which were rejected - turning errors into recoverable, in-loop feedback." Convergence is handled by two dedicated tools - a Winn-Underwood-Gilliland shortcut method that initialises a rigorous column "avoiding the solver failures that commonly attend an uninitialized column", and a bisection design-specification tool - and "convergence status is returned as a plain-language summary with an explicit converged/not-converged flag, with raw solver codes kept in a separate diagnostic field". The analysis tools "enforce a strict honesty discipline: an unconverged simulation is refused rather than costed, and an infeasible purity target is reported as such rather than answered with a fabricated optimum." Malformed requests never reach the simulator at all: "requests that do not match a tool's declared input format are rejected before they reach the simulator"

what_it_drives: density functional theory and molecular dynamics calculations used as physics verifiers, and a particle-swarm search over a 56-dimensional chemical latent space
failure_handling: the agents are described as reasoning about simulation failures and adapting search strategies, with no mechanism stated

what_it_drives: the BESTOpt building-HVAC-distributed-energy-resource simulation platform, scaling from single-zone buildings to a 30-building residential cluster
failure_handling: not stated

what_it_drives: a validated ensemble Bayesian-optimisation tool and the deep-ensemble models it tunes, on the OECD/NEA critical heat flux benchmark
failure_handling: the supervisor coordinates the agents through explicit invocation, error-detection and termination protocols, confining model stochasticity to recoverable workflow steps

what_it_drives: Bayesian optimisation pipelines on the Ax Platform, emitted as generated Python code from Honegumi skeletons
failure_handling: not stated

what_it_drives: a fine-tuned quantum-chemistry property model used as a frozen forward verifier against an inverse generator, inside a replayable state graph
failure_handling: not stated; the frozen forward model acts as a verifier and reward signal rather than an error handler

what_it_drives: machine-learning property models for magnesium hydride dehydrogenation and a genetic algorithm performing exploratory inverse design over them
failure_handling: not stated

what_it_drives: seven independently developed finite-element solvers - FEniCSx, deal.II, 4C Multiphysics, NGSolve, scikit-fem, Kratos Multiphysics and DUNE-fem - plus mesh generation and multi-solver coupling
failure_handling: not stated

what_it_drives: quantum chemistry calculations submitted as Slurm jobs on an HPC cluster, across conformer searches, production runs and multi-method validation
failure_handling: the system is reported to have identified and autocorrected cluster failures and to include failure diagnosis among its automated operations, with no mechanism stated

what_it_drives: genomics tools dispatched as Slurm batch jobs on a production cluster through hash-verified run specifications
failure_handling: tampered execution plans are rejected before scheduling; nothing is stated about a failed or non-converging job

what_it_drives: quantum chemistry tool nodes dispatched in parallel by a deterministic executor, up to 200 concurrently from a single planning call
failure_handling: not stated

what_it_drives: an open-source Python Tanabe-Sugano diagram solver computing term energies, comparing configurations and fitting measured absorption bands
failure_handling: not stated

what_it_drives: LAMMPS reverse non-equilibrium molecular dynamics runs on randomly generated face-centred-cubic supercells of a cobalt-chromium-nickel alloy, with equilibration and production stages
failure_handling: a reliability filter combining uncertainty thresholding and split-branch temperature-gradient fitting distinguishes physically meaningful candidates from numerical artefacts

what_it_drives: LAMMPS input scripts and runs on the Argonne Carbon HPC cluster - Atomsk-generated crystal structures, EAM potential files fetched from the NIST repository, and LAMMPS relaxation, elastic-constant, phonon and melting simulations, with Phonopy and OVITO post-processing
failure_handling: the LAMMPS input reviewer agent "monitors the output logs from each simulation and parses for known failure signatures, including invalid commands (e.g., misnamed keywords or deprecated syntax), numerical instabilities (e.g., atom loss, box deformation) and missing potential files or incorrect atom types", then collaborates with the relevant task agent to correct and resubmit; a pre-flight function check refuses to write an input file unless a valid potential and structure file are present; and a vision agent inspects OVITO frames and resubmits at higher temperature or longer runtime when the solid-liquid ratio or full melting is not reached

what_it_drives: EnergyPlus 23.2 IDF files for six named Purdue University campus buildings - geometry written from street-level reconstruction, then equipment density, lighting density, infiltration and schedule parameters rewritten each iteration and re-simulated through an Optuna TPE loop at 25 EnergyPlus runs per pass
failure_handling: three safeguards sit between the LLM and the optimiser: "Hard physical clamping. Every suggested [min, max] range is truncated to the global physical limits stored in the configuration file (e.g. equipment density [1, 200] W/m2; infiltration [0.01, 2.0] ACH)"; "Inverted-range detection. If clamping collapses the range to min >= max, the LLM suggestion is discarded and the global configuration bounds are used instead"; and "JSON parse fallback. If the LLM response fails to parse, a dedicated JSONDecodeError handler, followed by a general Exception catch, substitutes the global bounds for any affected parameter." A two-tier human-in-the-loop gate routes any building with confidence < 0.7 or a non-empty concerns list to a human-review queue, and "the HITL flag triggers review rather than automatic rollback". Non-convergence is bounded by MAX_ITER = 10 and an early stop when two consecutive CV(RMSE) improvements fall below 0.5%
